headline_marked: Intel fixes [[18A wafer-to-wafer yield issues]] with 15,000 wafers/month
headline: Intel fixes 18A wafer-to-wafer yield issues with 15,000 wafers/month
summary: Intel resolves 18A process yield variability issues, boosting production. Report claims 15,000 wafers/month at both sites.
details: Intel has resolved wafer-to-wafer yield variability issues with its 18A process technology, according to a report from BlueFin Research Partners. This development is expected to bring consistent and predictable yield improvements for products made using the 1.8nm-class node.

The report claims that Intel now has a capacity of around 30,000 wafer starts per month across its D1X development fab in Oregon and Fab 52 high-volume fab in Arizona. This is a solid result at this point of the ramp cycle.

Fixing wafer-to-wafer yield issues does not necessarily mean overall yield is where Intel wants it to be, but it allows for consistent yield improvement. Intel aims to continue this practice with its next-generation 14A (1.4nm) fabrication process.
caption:
Can Intel's 18A process technology finally deliver on its promises? 15,000 wafers/month produced.

Intel has resolved wafer-to-wafer yield variability issues with its 18A process technology, according to a report from BlueFin Research Partners. This development is expected to bring consistent and predictable yield improvements for products made using the 1.8nm-class node.

The report claims that Intel now has a capacity of around 30,000 wafer starts per month across its D1X development fab in Oregon and Fab 52 high-volume fab in Arizona. This is a solid result at this point of the ramp cycle.

Fixing wafer-to-wafer yield issues does not necessarily mean overall yield is where Intel wants it to be, but it allows for consistent yield improvement. Intel aims to continue this practice with its next-generation 14A (1.4nm) fabrication process.
